aj: Quick intake — Acme (sales prospect) asked for a blended offering: reserved capacity + hosted burst. They want an anchor per-token number and clarity on how overages are calculated. They specifically call out embeddings-heavy workload and want an SLA.
 tayla: Got it. Can you share expected token volumes and region? Two things product needs to scope: pricing bands (per-token tiers) and launch criteria for a bespoke blended offer (billing, SLA, contract). Also confirm if they need dedicated GPUs all day or just business hours.
 aj: They provided a sample: ~6M tokens/day, ~80% embeddings (avg 512 tokens/req), 20% chat. Preferred region: us-west. They want a guaranteed 99.9% uptime on dedicated path and fallback to hosted when dedicated is saturated.
 jonas: Heads up — runtime billing quirks: our embedding pipeline rounds up small requests to a 64-token minimum unless batched; that materially affects unit economics for lots of tiny embeds. Dedicated unit cost also differs based on quantization profile. Fallback path adds ~10-20ms and may flip to a different model (cost delta).
 kevin: For modelling: simple approach is weighted blended rate = (reserved_rate * commit_tokens + hosted_rate * burst_tokens) / total_tokens. Example sketch: reserved commit 3M tokens/day at 30% off list, hosted list for overage. We should also consider a monthly subscription for SLA and an explicit overage multiplier (e.g., 1.25x list for burst).
 tayla: Proposed product plan / acceptance criteria:
  - Pricing: define 3 per-token bands (<=1M, 1-5M, >5M) with anchored discounts for reserved commit.
  - Overage policy: specify billing unit (token rounding), multiplier, and cadence (daily vs monthly reconciliation).
  - Engineering: verify billing rounding/aggregation and tagging for routing (dedicated vs hosted).
  - Legal/Finance: contract clause for SLA and invoice line templates.
  - Launch criteria: pricing approved by finance, billing integration tested in staging with a sample invoice, and customer sign-off on SLA + routing behavior.
 tayla: Can we get the above captured as a product backlog item? Tag it needs-pricing-review and add acceptance tests (billing records, simulated failover to hosted).
 aj: I can create the intake ticket and attach their usage sample. Can we get a preliminary anchor number by EOD Friday? :grimacing:
 jonas: I can run a quick cost sim using their sample and our cost model — will aim for Thursday EOD.
 kevin: I'll produce a blended-pricing spreadsheet and sample invoice line items by Thursday.
 billing-bot: New ticket created: PRD-8421 "per-token tiering request — ACME" assigned to tayla.
 tayla: Thanks — moving PRD-8421 to triage. I'll add acceptance criteria and assign engineering validation to jonas. If anyone has explicit tokenization samples, drop them into the ticket.
 aj: Thanks everyone, adding the sample now"
